summary: Shared per-session dedup state for all three recall hooks: readSeen / writeSeen / idsInPage / seenArgs. Exists because 61% of injections re-showed a note the same session already had; the ids are passed to `kb search --seen` which drops them from the page it would otherwise render. Two decisions that look arbitrary and are not: (1) the state file sits under os.tmpdir(), NOT literal /tmp — literal /tmp is reserved for the find_nudge state file, which the nudge handler reads back by an agreed literal path, so putting this there would invite collisions; (2) the set resets on the TRANSCRIPT SHRINKING rather than on a clock, because after a compact the session id is unchanged but the context is gone, making a previously-shown note genuinely absent again. Hosts that pass no transcript path never reset, which is the safe direction — dedup still holds for the session. idsInPage parses `→ open: …/notes/<id>.md` out of rendered text, so this couples to the pointer-page format: change that rendering and dedup silently stops recording. Every function swallows its own errors, so a failure leaves dedup OFF rather than blocking recall.

summary: Per-session recall dedup state shared by all three recall hooks (kb-recall.mjs, cursor-kb-recall.mjs, codex-kb-recall.mjs each import readSeen/writeSeen/idsInPage/seenArgs) so their behaviour cannot drift; created 2026-07-30 after the dedup shipped Claude-only and Cursor/Codex kept re-showing notes. State lives at os.tmpdir()/coldstart-recall-seen-<sid>.json — deliberately NOT literal /tmp, which is reserved for the find_nudge state file the nudge handler reads back by an agreed literal path. The seen set resets when the transcript file SHRINKS (a compact) rather than on a clock, because after a compact the session id is unchanged but the context is gone, so a previously-shown note is genuinely absent again; a host that exposes no transcript path (ephemeral Codex runs) simply never resets, which is the safe direction. idsInPage parses ids back out of the RENDERED pointer page via the '-> open: .../<id>.md' line, so the hooks need no structured output from the CLI. Every function is fail-open: any error leaves dedup off rather than blocking recall. Verified E2E on all three hooks this session: inject -> silent -> transcript shrinks -> inject, and inject -> silent with no transcript path.

summary: Per-session recall dedup state shared by all three recall hooks (kb-recall.mjs, cursor-kb-recall.mjs, codex-kb-recall.mjs import readSeen/writeSeen/idsInPage/seenArgs) so their behaviour cannot drift. State lives at os.tmpdir()/coldstart-recall-seen-<sid>.json as {ids, since, ts}, deliberately NOT literal /tmp, which is reserved for the find_nudge state file. readSeen(sid, root) returns the ids shown since the last compaction (24h TTL) UNIONED with ids this session wrote at or after `since`, read from the tail of .coldstart/notebook/.metrics/capture.jsonl (`kb write --session` write events), because a note the agent just wrote was the most common wrong injection. The ONLY reset is resetSeen, called by the host compaction hook recall-compact.mjs; it empties ids and moves `since` to now. It does NOT look at the transcript: Claude Code transcripts are append-only (a compact appends a compact_boundary line), so the earlier 'transcript shrank' reset never fired in real use. idsInPage parses ids out of the RENDERED pointer page via the '-> open: .../<id>.md' line. Every function is fail-open.
